units.source_text: 雪山童子遇鬼，向之求法。

en.t: The Snow Mountain youth met a demon and asked him for the Dharma.

units.source_text: 鬼唱曰：“诸行无常，是生灭法。”

en.t: The demon chanted, “All conditioned things are impermanent; this is the law of arising and passing away.”

units.source_text: 下半尚有二句，鬼因肚饥，唱不出了。

en.t: There were still two lines in the second half, but because the demon was hungry, he could not chant them.
The youth asked, “What do you want to eat?”
The demon said, “I want to eat blood and flesh.”

units.source_text: 童子曰：“教我下半，我身即与你吃。”

en.t: The youth said, “Teach me the second half, and I will at once give you my body to eat.”

units.source_text: 鬼续唱曰：“生灭灭已，寂灭为乐。”

en.t: The demon continued chanting, “When arising and passing away have ceased, tranquil extinction is bliss.”

units.source_text: 童子乃将此四句偈书之石壁，投身喂鬼。

en.t: The youth then wrote these four lines of verse on a stone wall and threw himself down to feed the demon.

units.source_text: 此故事见《阿含经》及《涅槃经》。

en.t: This story appears in the Agama Sutras and the Nirvana Sutra.
